## Best portable power station for camping

The right size depends on your trip. Most car and tent campers do well with a **250–500Wh** unit, which runs phones, lights, camera batteries, and a CPAP for a few nights. Bigger trips or a 12V fridge need a 1,000Wh+ unit, which is heavier and costs more. [2][3]

### Picks by trip type

| Trip | Pick | Specs | Price (per source) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weekend, easiest to pack | **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus** | 288Wh, 300W AC, ~8.3 lb | ~$249 [2] |
| Best value | **EcoFlow River 3 Plus** | 286Wh, 600W AC, ~9.9 lb | ~$269–299 [2] |
| Budget | **Bluetti EB3A** | 268Wh, 600W AC, ~10.1 lb | ~$179 [2] |
| Long trips, built-in lantern | **Anker SOLIX C300** | 288Wh, 300W AC (600W surge), ~9.3 lb | ~$199 [2] |
| Bigger off-grid trips | **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** | 890Wh, 1,800W AC, ~25 lb | ~$530 on sale [3] |
| Multi-day off-grid | **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** | 1,710Wh usable, 2,200W AC, ~39 lb | Under $900 on Amazon [3] |
| Rugged, long weekends | **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** | 1,536Wh, 1,800W AC, IP65, ~40 lb | $1,079 at Amazon [5] |

Sources: [2] PowerStationGearLab, [3] OutdoorGearLab, [5] WIRED. Prices were snapshots at the time of each article, so check current prices.

**A note on the Explorer 300 Plus:** PowerStationGearLab reports that Jackery's U.S. site no longer lists it. It is still sold through Amazon and other retailers, and Jackery has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. [2]

### Bluetti AC180 (larger option with a discount code)

The AC180 has 1,152Wh, LiFePO4 cells rated for 3,500+ cycles, and an 1,800W AC output. It weighs about 16 kg and carries a 5-year warranty. The list price is $499. A third-party site reports that code AFF5OFF takes $24.95 off, for about $474.05. [1]

For the other models, I could not find verified direct product links in these results. Search the model name on Amazon or the brand's U.S. site, or use the "Check price" links on the review pages above.

### Tips for camping use

- **CPAP:** Turn the humidifier off. It can roughly triple the machine's power draw. With it off, a 288Wh unit runs most CPAPs for 3–5 nights. [2]
- **Rough energy budget:** About 10Wh per phone charge, 30–60Wh per CPAP night, and about 5Wh per lantern night. [2]
- **Weight vs. capacity:** For camping, a unit you can carry easily usually matters more than the largest one. [2]
- **Solar:** Most of these pair with portable solar panels, which extend trips. [3][7]
